title: Le défi de Sophie Germain : ses travaux sur les vibrations des surfaces élastiques
venue: Thèse de doctorat, Université de Lorraine (dir. Philippe Nabonnand et Olivier Bruneau), soutenue le 13 décembre 2022 — Annexe D : transcription des trois mémoires
note: The only transcription of the three prize memoirs, 120 pages of annex, made from the originals at the Archives des prix. Open access on HAL and on the university's server, under the standard thesis notice: « soumis à la propriété intellectuelle de l'auteur ». Read it there.
rights: Author's copyright; no Creative Commons licence. This site links and cites, and does not reproduce a line of the transcription — not even to seed its own reading of pages that are not online.

title: « Voici ce que j'ai trouvé » : Sophie Germain's grand plan to prove Fermat's Last Theorem
note: The paper that located the Fermat manuscripts by folio and read them as one plan. Its § 1.3 is the source of every piece on the Fermat cahier's page. Quotes the manuscripts in French with translation; its figures reproduce four pages of Français 9114.
rights: Elsevier journal; arXiv version under arXiv's perpetual non-exclusive licence. Linked and cited; figures not reproduced.

title: Sophie Germain, mathématicienne extraordinaire: a story stranger than fiction
note: A synthesis of what the manuscripts and the correspondence with Legendre and Gauss now show, sixteen years after the Historia paper. Which shelfmarks it draws on beyond those of 2010 has not been checked leaf by leaf here.
rights: arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence. Linked and cited.

title: Unpublished manuscripts of Sophie Germain and a revaluation of her work on Fermat's Last Theorem
venue: Archive for History of Exact Sciences 62, 349–392
note: Transcribes the Florence draft of the « Remarques » in full, the appendix to the 1804 letter to Gauss, and the letter of 12 May 1819 — the three texts on which the reassessment rests.
rights: Springer; not open access. Linked and cited, never copied.

title: The correspondence between Sophie Germain and Carl Friedrich Gauss
editors: Andrea Del Centina and Alessandra Fiocca
venue: Archive for History of Exact Sciences 66, 585–700
note: The whole correspondence in both directions, with the mathematical notes enclosed in her letters published for the first time — results on power residues nobody had attributed to her.
rights: Springer; not open access. Linked and cited, never copied.

title: Letters of Sophie Germain preserved in Florence
note: Nine letters from the Fondo Palagi-Libri: six to Libri, and drafts to Poinsot, Legendre and Lagrange that were unknown before.
rights: Elsevier; open archive after embargo. Linked and cited.

title: Sophie Germain: an essay in the history of the theory of elasticity
editors: Louis L. Bucciarelli and Nancy Dworsky
venue: Studies in the History of Modern Science 6, Reidel, Dordrecht
note: The mathematical biography of the elasticity work, drawn from the BnF volumes and the Académie's dossiers. Which leaves of which volume it cites is recorded in its notes and has not been carried into this catalogue.

title: Mécanique et théorie des surfaces : les travaux de Sophie Germain
note: The French reassessment of the memoirs, a generation before Grun.
rights: Elsevier; open archive. Linked and cited.

title: Recherches sur la théorie des surfaces élastiques
venue: Paris, Veuve Courcier — the third memoir, reworked and printed at her own expense
note: Her own printing of the prize memoir, revised. Public domain; on Gallica, the Internet Archive and Wikisource. The relation to the 1815 manuscript is one of revision, not identity — Grun's Annexe C compares the memoirs — so the mapping is « likely », not certain.
rights: Public domain. May be quoted, framed and transcribed freely.

title: Remarques sur la nature, les bornes et l'étendue de la question des surfaces élastiques, et équation générale de ces surfaces
note: Her reply to the criticism of the « Recherches ». No manuscript of it is located in the volumes listed here.

title: Cinq lettres de Sophie Germain à Charles-Frédéric Gauss, publiées d'après les originaux possédés par la Société royale des sciences de Göttingen
venue: Berlin, Archiv der Mathematik und Physik
note: Five of the ten letters, in the public domain. The first edition of any of her letters to Gauss.
rights: Public domain. On Gallica and the Internet Archive.

title: Œuvres philosophiques de Sophie Germain, suivies de pensées et de lettres inédites
note: The « Considérations générales » (Français 9117), the « Pensées », and a selection of letters. Public domain. The volume of 1833 by her nephew Lherbette is the first edition of the essay.
